findings.body: The supplied full-suite check remains failed: 9 failed, 1613 passed, 7 skipped. One failure is directly verifiable: tests/test_rules.py:44–45 requires test_<n>_<rule>, but all 12 tests in this file and the test in tests/test_starter_names_survive_branch_cleanup.py have unnumbered names. The required workflow runs the entire suite (.github/workflows/forge.yml:39). Resolve this naming incompatibility and the reported board-text, approval/start-publication, machine-view-count and merge-enable failures before claiming the required check passes. The 83 passing related tests do not clear these failures.

findings.body: The previous P2 remains open. A teammate without a local story worktree skips this approval check, even when the published plan has a passing cold read but has not been approved. Consequently, next offers assigned parts as able to start, while task start refuses them at src/forge/task.py:241–245. Published plans awaiting renewed approval have the same mismatch. Check the selected published state's approval hash against the reconciled plan before offering starts. The assignment-discovery tests approve their plans and therefore do not catch this case.
findings.title: Check approval before offering starts from a published draft

findings.body: The previous P2 remains open. Removing an unmerged item's branches and worktree leaves its immutable start tag. Fix name selection considers only branches and merged state (src/forge/task.py:336–339), so restarting the same slug creates a worktree and commits its state before this update-ref fails because the tag already exists. Reusing removed story or task names has the same problem. Copied-plan tasks can also collide with the retained forge-plan tag at task.py:123, leaving an unfinished checkout. Reserve retained names during selection or detect both tag collisions before creating work, while preserving the original references.
findings.title: Account for retained tags before reusing an abandoned branch name

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow (2026-10-09): keep who started an item through a stacked fix replayed onto the default branch and through a story's first part that starts from the default branch and copies the plan, with a test for each; nothing else changes.

why: On a team, started work stays on the laptop where it began until its first close, so teammates can't see who is working on what and two developers can start the same part; no person is shown on any item. Owner decision 2026-10-09: starting is the claim, with git as the one record
